Returns a pointer to one record of the class equipment table loaded from PROEQU.DAT: the item types the class is allowed to equip.

Algorithm:
Multiplies class_index by 6, the PROEQU.DAT record stride, adds the table base pointer held in the global at 0x00063fe4, spills the sum to a stack local and reloads it into EAX as the return value. fdps_load_data_tables@00018930 fills that global at startup by loading "ProEqu.dat" through fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit, so the pointer is valid from startup until teardown. There is no null check on the base pointer and no bounds check on the index: the table holds 36 records, covering class codes 0x00..0x23, while class codes run to 0x27, so 0x24-0x27 address memory past its end. No unit that reaches the only caller carries such a class: every unit on the shop, village-equip and player-phase paths has a class from FRIAPRDA.DAT or RANKUP.DAT, at most 0x19.

The record is six bytes from the same value space as byte +0 of an ITEM.DAT record, the item type. They are a variable-length set, stored in ascending order and right-padded with 0xff -- not six fixed slots: in the shipped table a given type sits at whichever position the sorting puts it in, and records run from one type used (class 0x1a, 0e ff ff ff ff ff) to all six (classes 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0f..0x12 and 0x20). The only caller, fdps_unit_can_equip_item, scans all six positions identically and returns 1 when one of them equals the type of the item it was asked about, which makes this table the "which item types may this class equip" list. The 0xff padding never matches because no ITEM.DAT record carries type 0xff; one code that does appear in the table, 0x2d in the records for classes 0x20 and 0x21, is carried by no item either.

Parameters:
  class_index -- the unit's class code, taken straight from byte +0x20 of its 0x50-byte unit record. Passed raw, not incremented: the PROMAP.DAT accessor fdps_get_class_record is fed class code + 1, this one is not.

Returns:
  Pointer to the class's 6-byte record, i.e. base + class_index * 6. It is address arithmetic only and is never NULL while the table is loaded, whether or not the index is in range.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only data reference is the game global at 0x00063fe4, written by the game's own table loader, and its only reference is a static call from game logic]

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious rewrite diverges. (1) PROEQU.DAT is indexed by the raw class code, while its neighbour PROMAP.DAT is indexed by class code + 1 -- the callers of fdps_get_class_record that look up a particular unit INC its byte +0x20 before calling (all but fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, which omits it, an original defect), the caller of this one does not. Writing the equipment lookup by analogy with the class lookup and adding 1 shifts every class's permitted-equipment list by one record. The table is also 36 records against 40 class codes, so classes 0x24-0x27 read past its end and this accessor does not check. (2) The unused positions of a record hold 0xff, not 0, and the scan in fdps_unit_can_equip_item has no sentinel test at all -- it compares all six. Treating 0 as the empty marker is the intuitive reading and it is wrong: 0x00 is the type byte of the 25 all-zero ITEM.DAT records 0xE2-0xFA and of no item with content, so a table or a comparison written that way would let every class with an unused position -- all but 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0f..0x12 and 0x20 -- equip all of them.

Moves a unit toward a requested destination tile: traces a path, retargets to the furthest walkable tile when the direct route is blocked, then picks the reachable tile nearest the target and animates the move.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; body is entirely game-domain]
Evidence: Calls only game routines - fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_get_class_record, fdps_move_path_trace, fdps_map_load_tile_info, fdps_animate_move_path - and reads the map probe result at DAT_00069d0c. malloc/free/abs are consumed, not joined. All callers are battle and map code. Not crt or ail (no library byte match, no vendor state area), not binary_artifact (945-byte body with a real frame).
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; no library symbol identified, and none exists to identify.
Boundary: 000119e0-00011d90, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 to matching epilogue 89 ec 5d 5f 5e 5b c3; the 15 bytes after are lea-form alignment padding before fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles.
Signature: __cdecl, int (int dest_x, int dest_y, int unit_index, int side_select) at [ebp+0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x20], caller-cleaned (add esp,0x10 at every call site), result in EAX. The fourth argument is a side truth value, not a mode: it reaches only fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control (00010be9..00010c07, marks the units whose side byte at +6 is non-zero when the argument is 0) and fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles (0001197a..0001199d, which reads it with the opposite polarity).

Algorithm:
1. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) supplies tile x at +0x00, tile y at +0x01, a class index at +0x20 and a movement/terrain cost selector at +0x3b.
2. fdps_get_class_record(class_index + 1) yields the movement context; malloc(100) is the step buffer (one direction code per step) and malloc(0x800) is the reachable-tile list (x,y byte pairs).
3. Mark the opposing units' zones of control with fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(side_select), then build the movement cost map with fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range(ctx, x, y, cost_selector) - only the flood builds the cost map, the mark does not - and path from the unit to (dest_x, dest_y) with fdps_move_path_trace(x, y, step_buf, dest_x, dest_y, 0), which returns the step count or -1 for no path.
4. On failure, reset, flood with NO mark and an allowance of 100, and retry with the relaxed flag 1. If a relaxed path exists, reset, mark and flood again with the unit's real allowance (00011af4), then replay the relaxed path step by step (direction 0 = y+1, 1 = x-1, 2 = y-1, else x+1), probing each tile with fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and reading DAT_00069d0c. The last tile whose probe is not 0xff becomes the new destination - the request is retargeted to the furthest usable tile along the blocked route.
5. Rebuild the movement map, then narrow it with fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles(unit_index, side_select), which does the OPPOSITE of flooding the unit's reach: it stores the 0xff unreachable sentinel into the occupied units' cells, so the mover may cross them but may not stop on them. Collect the tiles that survive with fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles(tile_buf), which returns their count.
6. Scan those tiles and keep the one minimising |tx - dest_x| + |ty - dest_y|, breaking ties on the smaller ||dx| - |dy||.
7. Path to the chosen tile with the strict flag 0. If the step count is non-zero, fdps_animate_move_path(unit_index, step_buf, step_count) performs the move and the result is 1; otherwise 0.
8. Free both buffers and return.

Grid setup rounds: the grid is set up up to five times. Round 1 at 00011a5a does not reset first, so it inherits whatever the caller staged. Round 2 at 00011aaa resets and floods with NO mark and a literal allowance of 100. When round 2 finds a route, the retarget rebuild at 00011af4 resets + marks + floods with the unit's real allowance before the probe loop, the same setup as round 4. Rounds 3 (00011bc6) and 4 (00011cef) reset + mark + flood, and only round 3 calls fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles. The retarget rebuild and round 4 aside, the rounds are NOT interchangeable: collapsing them into one shared setup would change which tiles the walk may cross and which it may finish on.

Rebuild note: the three MP-regeneration passes are independent -- unit 4 (0xa6, else 0xa7, found entry equipped), unit 8 (0xb1, equipped), then every unit holding 0xb3 (merely held) -- and the shard pass does not skip units 4 and 8, so a unit qualifying for both regenerates twice in one turn (only once if the first restore brings MP up to its maximum, since fdps_unit_restore_mp clamps and the second pass then sees mp_current == mp_max). All three passes test only byte +0x05 == 0 and MP != max MP; none tests the side byte +0x06 or the poison/paralysis timers +0x25/+0x26. Merging them into one 'at most once per unit' loop, or reusing the rest sweep's guard (side 2, flags & 0x81, timers), changes the result.
